questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why is dimensional analysis useful?

options.A: It can prove an equation is correct
options.B: It can check equation consistency, help derive possible relationships and convert units, but it cannot determine dimensionless numerical constants or prove an equation correct
options.C: It determines the exact value of constants
options.D: It replaces the need for experiments

questions.explanation: It can check equation consistency, help derive possible relationships and convert units, but it cannot determine dimensionless numerical constants or prove an equation correct.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the difference between mass and weight?

options.A: Mass is measured in newtons; weight is measured in kilograms
options.B: Mass is the amount of matter and is measured in kilograms; weight is gravitational force and is measured in newtons

questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter and is measured in kilograms; weight is gravitational force and is measured in newtons.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the difference between precision and accuracy?

options.A: Accuracy is closeness among repeated measurements; precision is closeness to the true value
options.B: Accuracy is closeness to the true or accepted value; precision is closeness among repeated measurements
options.D: Precision applies only to length measurements

questions.explanation: Accuracy is closeness to the true or accepted value; precision is closeness among repeated measurements.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Newton's first law of motion state?

options.B: A body remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted on by a net external force
options.C: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
options.D: Energy cannot be created or destroyed

questions.explanation: Newton's first law states that a body remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted on by a net external force; this is the law of inertia.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Newton's second law of motion state?

options.A: An object at rest stays at rest
options.B: The net force equals the rate of change of momentum; for constant mass, F = ma
options.C: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction

questions.explanation: Newton's second law states that the net force equals the rate of change of momentum; for constant mass, F = ma.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Newton's third law of motion state?

options.B: For every action force there is an equal and opposite reaction force; the two forces act on different bodies
options.C: Objects remain at rest unless acted upon

questions.explanation: Newton's third law states that for every action force there is an equal and opposite reaction force; the two forces act on different bodies.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the law of universal gravitation state?

options.A: Every two masses attract each other with a force proportional to the sum of their masses
options.B: Every two masses attract each other with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres
options.C: Gravity only acts on large objects

questions.explanation: The law of universal gravitation states that every two masses attract each other with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the law of conservation of energy state?

options.A: Energy can be created but not destroyed
options.B: Energy cannot be created or destroyed in an isolated system; it can be transferred or transformed from one form to another
options.C: Energy is always lost as heat
options.D: Energy can be destroyed but not created

questions.explanation: The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed in an isolated system; it can be transferred or transformed from one form to another.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the law of conservation of momentum state?

options.B: The total momentum of an isolated system remains constant when the net external force or impulse is zero
options.D: Momentum equals mass times velocity squared

questions.explanation: The law of conservation of momentum states that the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant when the net external force or impulse is zero.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Archimedes' principle state?

options.A: A body immersed in a fluid experiences a downward force
options.B: A body wholly or partly immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced

questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle states that a body wholly or partly immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Pascal's law state?

options.B: A pressure change applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished throughout the fluid and to the container walls, in the ideal static-fluid model

questions.explanation: Pascal's law states that a pressure change applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished throughout the fluid and to the container walls, in the ideal static-fluid model.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Bernoulli's principle state?

options.A: Higher fluid speed is associated with higher pressure
options.B: For steady, incompressible, non-viscous flow along a streamline, higher fluid speed is associated with lower static pressure when elevation is unchanged
options.C: Pressure is always constant in a fluid
options.D: Fluid speed decreases with decreasing pressure

questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle states that for steady, incompressible, non-viscous flow along a streamline, higher fluid speed is associated with lower static pressure when elevation is unchanged; the full energy equation includes elevation and velocity terms.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Boyle's law state?

options.A: For a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, pressure is directly proportional to volume
options.B: For a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume
options.C: For a fixed amount of gas at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to temperature
options.D: For a fixed amount of gas at constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to temperature

questions.explanation: Boyle's law states that for a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Charles's law state?

options.A: For a fixed amount of gas at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature
options.B: For a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume
options.C: For a fixed amount of gas at constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to temperature
options.D: Equal volumes of gases contain equal numbers of molecules

questions.explanation: Charles's law states that for a fixed amount of gas at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Gay-Lussac's pressure law state?

options.A: For a fixed amount of gas at constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature
options.B: For a fixed amount of gas at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to temperature
options.C: For a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume
options.D: Equal volumes of gases contain equal numbers of molecules

questions.explanation: Gay-Lussac's pressure law states that for a fixed amount of gas at constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature: P₁/T₁ = P₂/T₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Avogadro's law state?

options.A: At the same temperature and pressure, equal volumes of ideal gases contain equal numbers of molecules
options.B: Pressure is inversely proportional to volume
options.C: Volume is directly proportional to pressure
options.D: Temperature is directly proportional to pressure

questions.explanation: Avogadro's law states that at the same temperature and pressure, equal volumes of ideal gases contain equal numbers of molecules; volume is proportional to amount of gas at fixed temperature and pressure.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Ohm's law state?

options.A: Current is inversely proportional to voltage
options.B: For a conductor under constant physical conditions, current is proportional to potential difference: V = IR
options.D: Voltage equals current squared times resistance

questions.explanation: Ohm's law states that for a conductor under constant physical conditions, current is proportional to potential difference: V = IR.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Joule's law of heating state?

options.A: Heat produced is proportional to current only
options.B: Electrical energy converted to heat in a resistor is Q = I²RT
options.C: Heat produced is inversely proportional to resistance
options.D: Heat produced is independent of time

questions.explanation: Joule's law of heating states that electrical energy converted to heat in a resistor is Q = I²RT; equivalently Q = VIT for a suitable constant-voltage circuit.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction state?

options.A: Induced emf is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage
options.B: Induced emf is independent of magnetic flux
options.C: Induced emf is proportional to resistance
options.D: Induced emf is constant regardless of flux change

questions.explanation: Faraday's law states that the induced electromotive force is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage; the negative sign in the law represents Lenz's law.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Lenz's law state?

options.A: Induced current flows in a direction that enhances the change in magnetic flux
options.B: The induced current flows in a direction that opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it
options.D: Induced current depends only on resistance

questions.explanation: Lenz's law states that the induced current flows in a direction that opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the first law of thermodynamics state?

options.A: Entropy of an isolated system never decreases
options.B: Change in a system's internal energy equals heat added to the system minus work done by the system
options.C: Heat cannot flow from cold to hot

questions.explanation: The first law of thermodynamics states that change in a system's internal energy equals heat added to the system minus work done by the system, using that sign convention.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the second law of thermodynamics state?

options.A: Energy cannot be created or destroyed
options.B: The entropy of an isolated system never decreases; natural processes have a preferred direction and no heat engine can convert all absorbed heat into work in a cycle
options.C: Heat always flows from cold to hot

questions.explanation: The second law of thermodynamics states that the entropy of an isolated system never decreases; natural processes have a preferred direction and no heat engine can convert all absorbed heat into work in a cycle.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the third law of thermodynamics state?

options.B: The entropy of a perfect crystal approaches zero as its temperature approaches absolute zero; absolute zero cannot be reached by a finite sequence of processes
options.C: Heat engines cannot convert all heat into work
options.D: Energy is conserved in all processes

questions.explanation: The third law of thermodynamics states that the entropy of a perfect crystal approaches zero as its temperature approaches absolute zero; absolute zero cannot be reached by a finite sequence of processes.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the zeroth law of thermodynamics state?

options.A: Entropy of an isolated system never decreases
options.B: If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other
options.C: Energy cannot be created or destroyed

questions.explanation: The zeroth law states that if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other; this underlies temperature measurement.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the laws of reflection?

options.A: The angle of incidence is greater than the angle of reflection
options.B: The incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in one plane; the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
options.D: Reflection only occurs on rough surfaces

questions.explanation: The laws of reflection state that the incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in one plane; the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What do the laws of refraction state?

options.A: The angle of incidence always equals the angle of refraction
options.B: The incident ray, refracted ray and normal lie in one plane; Snell's law relates the sines of the angles to the refractive indices

questions.explanation: The laws of refraction state that the incident ray, refracted ray and normal lie in one plane; Snell's law relates the sines of the angles to the refractive indices: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is refractive index?

options.A: The ratio of the speed of light in a medium to its speed in vacuum
options.B: The ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its phase speed in a medium
options.C: The angle of refraction divided by the angle of incidence
options.D: The intensity of light in a medium

questions.explanation: Refractive index is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its phase speed in a medium; it describes how light propagates and bends at an interface.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Mendel's law of segregation state?

options.A: Alleles of different genes always assort together
options.B: The two alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation, so each gamete receives one allele; fertilisation restores the pair
options.C: One allele always dominates the other
options.D: Genes never separate during gamete formation

questions.explanation: Mendel's law of segregation states that the two alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation, so each gamete receives one allele; fertilisation restores the pair.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Mendel's law of independent assortment state?

options.B: Alleles of different genes assort independently during gamete formation when the genes are unlinked or sufficiently far apart

questions.explanation: Mendel's law of independent assortment states that alleles of different genes assort independently during gamete formation when the genes are unlinked or sufficiently far apart; linked genes can deviate.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Mendel's law of dominance state?

options.B: In a simple heterozygote, one allele may determine the phenotype over another; dominance is not universal
options.C: Recessive alleles are always more common

questions.explanation: Mendel's law of dominance states that in a simple heterozygote, one allele may determine the phenotype over another; dominance is not universal and does not mean an allele is more common or better.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the law of conservation of mass state?

options.A: Mass is always lost in chemical reactions
options.B: In ordinary chemical reactions in a closed system, total mass of reactants equals total mass of products
options.C: Mass can be created from energy

questions.explanation: The law of conservation of mass states that in ordinary chemical reactions in a closed system, total mass of reactants equals total mass of products; mass-energy equivalence matters in nuclear processes.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the law of definite proportions state?

options.B: A pure chemical compound contains its constituent elements in fixed proportions by mass, regardless of its source or preparation

questions.explanation: The law of definite proportions states that a pure chemical compound contains its constituent elements in fixed proportions by mass, regardless of its source or preparation.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the law of multiple proportions state?

options.A: Elements always combine in a 1:1 ratio
options.B: When two elements form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in small whole-number ratios
options.D: Mass is lost in chemical reactions

questions.explanation: The law of multiple proportions states that when two elements form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in small whole-number ratios.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the law of reciprocal proportions state?

options.A: Elements always combine in fixed ratios
options.B: The masses of two elements that separately combine with a fixed mass of a third element are related to the ratio in which they combine with each other, or a simple multiple of it
options.C: All compounds contain the same elements
options.D: Mass is conserved in nuclear reactions

questions.explanation: The law of reciprocal proportions states that the masses of two elements that separately combine with a fixed mass of a third element are related to the ratio in which they combine with each other, or a simple multiple of it.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the modern periodic law state?

options.A: Properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic masses
options.B: The physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers
options.C: Elements cannot be arranged in a table

questions.explanation: The modern periodic law states that the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the principle of natural selection?

options.B: Heritable variations that improve reproductive success in a particular environment tend to become more common over generations
options.D: Evolution occurs within a single lifetime

questions.explanation: The principle of natural selection states that heritable variations that improve reproductive success in a particular environment tend to become more common over generations; selection acts on variation in populations.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is biological evolution?

options.A: Change in an individual organism during its lifetime
options.B: Change in heritable characteristics of populations across generations, through mechanisms including mutation, natural selection, genetic drift, gene flow and recombination
options.C: The sudden appearance of new species

questions.explanation: Biological evolution is change in heritable characteristics of populations across generations, through mechanisms including mutation, natural selection, genetic drift, gene flow and recombination.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is adaptation?

options.A: A non-heritable change during an organism's lifetime
options.B: A heritable trait that increases reproductive success in a particular environment, or the evolutionary process by which such traits become more common
options.C: The ability to learn new skills
options.D: A temporary response to environmental stress

questions.explanation: Adaptation is a heritable trait that increases reproductive success in a particular environment, or the evolutionary process by which such traits become more common.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why is the principle of supply and demand not a scientific law?

options.B: It is an economic model or principle, not a physical or biological law; scientific laws in this syllabus refer to testable natural relationships
options.D: It applies to all natural phenomena

questions.explanation: The principle of supply and demand is an economic model or principle, not a physical or biological law; scientific laws in this syllabus refer to testable natural relationships.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the difference between a law and a principle?

options.A: A law is always more important than a principle
options.B: Usage varies by field; a law often describes a regular relationship, while a principle is a broad foundational rule or model
options.C: A principle is always mathematically proven

questions.explanation: Usage varies by field; a law often describes a regular relationship, while a principle is a broad foundational rule or model. Neither label alone determines scientific importance.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about pressure cooking?

options.A: Pressure cooking lowers the boiling point of water
options.B: Pressure cooking raises the boiling point of water by increasing pressure; it does not make water boil at a lower temperature
options.C: Pressure cooking has no effect on boiling point
options.D: Pressure cooking makes water boil at a lower temperature

questions.explanation: Pressure cooking raises the boiling point of water by increasing pressure; it does not make water boil at a lower temperature.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about a refrigerator?

options.B: A refrigerator transfers heat from inside to outside; it does not create cold
options.D: A refrigerator works without any energy input

questions.explanation: A refrigerator transfers heat from inside to outside; it does not create cold.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about microwave ovens?

options.B: Microwave ovens use non-ionising electromagnetic waves and do not make food radioactive

questions.explanation: Microwave ovens use non-ionising electromagnetic waves and do not make food radioactive.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about UV treatment in water purifiers?

options.B: UV treatment inactivates microorganisms but does not remove dissolved salts
options.C: UV treatment adds minerals to water
options.D: UV treatment removes all chemical contaminants

questions.explanation: UV treatment inactivates microorganisms but does not remove dissolved salts; RO reduces many dissolved substances but requires correct maintenance.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about induction cooktops?

options.A: Induction cooktops heat through a conventional exposed heating coil
options.B: Induction cooktops heat compatible cookware through induced currents
options.C: Induction cooktops work with any cookware

questions.explanation: Induction cooktops heat compatible cookware through induced currents; they do not work by a conventional exposed heating coil.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about fuse, MCB and earthing?

options.A: A fuse and MCB protect against electric shock; earthing protects against overcurrent
options.B: A fuse and MCB protect against overcurrent; earthing is a separate protective measure against electric shock
options.D: Fuses and MCBs are the same as earthing

questions.explanation: A fuse and MCB protect against overcurrent; earthing is a separate protective measure against electric shock.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about ammeter and voltmeter connection?

options.A: Ammeter-parallel, high resistance; voltmeter-series, low resistance
options.B: Ammeter-series, low resistance; voltmeter-parallel, high resistance

questions.explanation: Ammeter-series, low resistance; voltmeter-parallel, high resistance.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about hydrometer and lactometer?

options.A: Hydrometer measures milk purity; lactometer measures liquid density
options.B: Hydrometer measures liquid relative density; lactometer is a specialised hydrometer for milk and cannot establish purity alone

questions.explanation: Hydrometer measures liquid relative density; lactometer is a specialised hydrometer for milk and cannot establish purity alone.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about barometer, manometer and hygrometer?

options.B: Barometer-atmospheric pressure; manometer-pressure or pressure difference; hygrometer-humidity

questions.explanation: Barometer-atmospheric pressure; manometer-pressure or pressure difference; hygrometer-humidity.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about seismograph and seismogram?

options.A: Seismograph is the record; seismogram is the instrument
options.B: Seismograph records ground motion; seismogram is the record

questions.explanation: Seismograph records ground motion; seismogram is the record.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about ECG and EEG?

options.A: ECG records brain electrical activity; EEG records heart electrical activity
options.B: ECG records heart electrical activity; EEG records brain electrical activity

questions.explanation: ECG records heart electrical activity; EEG records brain electrical activity.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists the seven SI base units?

options.A: m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd
options.B: m, g, s, A, °C, mol, cd
options.C: m, kg, min, A, K, mol, lm
options.D: cm, kg, s, V, K, mol, cd

questions.explanation: SI base units: metre (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), ampere (A), kelvin (K), mole (mol) and candela (cd).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the quantity with its SI unit?

options.B: Force-joule; work-newton; power-pascal; pressure-watt; frequency-hertz

questions.explanation: Force: newton; work/energy: joule; power: watt; pressure: pascal; frequency: hertz.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the radiation quantity with its SI unit?

options.A: Radioactive activity-gray; absorbed dose-becquerel; equivalent dose-sievert
options.B: Radioactive activity-becquerel; absorbed dose-gray; equivalent/effective dose-sievert
options.C: Radioactive activity-sievert; absorbed dose-gray; equivalent dose-becquerel
options.D: Radioactive activity-becquerel; absorbed dose-sievert; equivalent dose-gray

questions.explanation: Radioactive activity: becquerel; absorbed dose: gray; equivalent/effective dose: sievert.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes mass and weight?

options.A: Mass is measured in newtons; weight is measured in kilograms
options.B: Mass is measured in kilograms; weight is a force measured in newtons

questions.explanation: Mass is measured in kg; weight is a force measured in N.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly gives the temperature conversion formulas?
questions.explanation: Temperature conversion: K = °C + 273.15; Fahrenheit = (9/5 × Celsius) + 32.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following unit conversion statements is correct?

options.A: 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J; 1 L = 10⁻³ m³; 1 standard atmosphere = 101,325 Pa
options.B: 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10³ J; 1 L = 10³ m³; 1 standard atmosphere = 100,000 Pa
options.C: 1 kWh = 1,000 J; 1 L = 1 m³; 1 standard atmosphere = 1,013 Pa
options.D: 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁹ J; 1 L = 10⁻² m³; 1 standard atmosphere = 10,325 Pa

questions.explanation: 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J; 1 L = 10⁻³ m³; 1 standard atmosphere = 101,325 Pa.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gas law assumes constant temperature?

options.B: Boyle's law

questions.explanation: Boyle's law assumes constant temperature; Charles's law assumes constant pressure; Gay-Lussac's law assumes constant volume.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gas law assumes constant pressure?

options.B: Charles's law

questions.explanation: Charles's law assumes constant pressure; Boyle's law assumes constant temperature; Gay-Lussac's law assumes constant volume.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gas law assumes constant volume?

options.B: Charles's law

questions.explanation: Gay-Lussac's law assumes constant volume; Boyle's law assumes constant temperature; Charles's law assumes constant pressure.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is an important limitation of Bernoulli's principle?

options.A: It applies to all real flows without exception
options.B: It has assumptions (steady, incompressible, non-viscous flow) and should not be applied indiscriminately to every real flow

questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle has assumptions; it should not be applied indiscriminately to every real flow.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the relationship between Faraday's law and Lenz's law?

options.A: Faraday's law concerns induced emf from changing magnetic flux; Lenz's law gives the opposing direction
options.B: Lenz's law concerns induced emf; Faraday's law gives the direction
options.D: Both laws deal with static electricity

questions.explanation: Faraday's law concerns induced emf from changing magnetic flux; Lenz's law gives the opposing direction.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: To which genes does Mendel's law of independent assortment apply straightforwardly?

options.B: Unlinked genes

questions.explanation: Mendel's independent assortment applies straightforwardly to unlinked genes; linked genes can show different inheritance patterns.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: On what basis is the modern periodic law based?

options.B: Atomic number

questions.explanation: Modern periodic law is based on atomic number, not atomic mass.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Do individuals evolve genetically during their own lifetime?

options.A: Yes, individuals evolve genetically during their lifetime
options.B: No, evolution is population change over generations; individuals do not evolve genetically during their own lifetime
options.C: Only animals evolve during their lifetime
options.D: Only plants evolve during their lifetime

questions.explanation: Evolution is population change over generations; individuals do not evolve genetically during their own lifetime.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Is dimensional consistency sufficient to prove a physical equation correct?

options.A: Yes, dimensional consistency proves an equation correct
options.B: No, dimensional consistency is necessary for a valid physical equation but is not sufficient to prove the equation correct
options.C: Dimensional analysis is not useful at all

questions.explanation: Dimensional consistency is necessary for a valid physical equation, but it is not sufficient to prove the equation correct.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What happens to the boiling point of water when pressure increases in a pressure cooker?

options.B: It increases above 100°C at normal sea-level pressure
options.D: Water does not boil in a pressure cooker

questions.explanation: Pressure raises the boiling point of water above 100°C at normal sea-level pressure, allowing food to cook at a higher temperature.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What happens to the boiling point of water at high altitude?

options.A: It increases because pressure is higher
options.B: It decreases because atmospheric pressure is lower
options.C: It remains the same as at sea level
options.D: Water cannot boil at high altitude

questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is lower at high altitude, so water boils at a lower temperature.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the role of the compressor in a refrigerator?

options.B: It compresses the refrigerant so it can condense and release heat outside the cabinet

questions.explanation: The refrigerant is compressed, condenses outside the cabinet and releases heat to the surroundings.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is dielectric heating in a microwave oven?

options.B: Heating caused by microwaves interacting with polar molecules and ions in food

questions.explanation: Microwaves interact with polar molecules and ions in food, producing dielectric heating.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why is heating in a microwave oven not always uniform?

options.B: Because microwave heating depends on food composition and geometry, so standing time and stirring may be needed

questions.explanation: Heating is not always uniform, so standing time and stirring may be needed.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the basic compatibility check for induction cookware?

options.B: A magnet sticking to the base is a useful basic compatibility check
options.C: The vessel should be made of glass
options.D: The vessel should be made of aluminium

questions.explanation: A magnet sticking to the base is a useful basic compatibility check, though manufacturer guidance should be followed.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the key components of a solar cooker that improve its performance?

options.A: Reflectors to concentrate sunlight and dark vessels to absorb radiation
options.B: Electric heating elements

questions.explanation: Reflectors may concentrate sunlight, while dark cooking vessels absorb radiation and insulation reduces heat loss.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which water purifier process uses a semipermeable membrane to reduce dissolved substances?

options.B: Reverse osmosis

questions.explanation: Reverse osmosis can reduce many dissolved substances, but performance depends on membrane, pretreatment, maintenance and water chemistry.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does activated carbon in water filters NOT reliably remove?

options.B: Organic compounds causing taste and odour
options.C: All microbes and dissolved inorganic salts

questions.explanation: Activated carbon adsorbs many organic compounds and can reduce chlorine, taste and odour; it does not reliably remove all microbes or dissolved inorganic salts.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is Joule heating in an electric kettle?

options.A: Conversion of electrical energy into heat by a resistive heating element
options.B: Conversion of heat into electricity
options.D: Conversion of mechanical energy into heat

questions.explanation: Electric current passes through a resistive heating element, converting electrical energy into heat by Joule heating.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How does an MCB differ from a fuse?

options.A: An MCB can generally be reset after the fault is corrected, while a fuse must be replaced
options.B: A fuse can be reset, while an MCB must be replaced
options.C: Both must be replaced after operation

questions.explanation: A miniature circuit breaker automatically opens a circuit during overcurrent conditions and can generally be reset after the fault is corrected.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the function of the third pin in a three-pin plug?

options.B: It supplies neutral current
options.C: It provides a protective earth connection

questions.explanation: The third pin provides a protective earth connection for appliances designed with Class I protection; live and neutral supply the circuit.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What produces the centrifugal effect in a washing machine spin cycle?

options.B: Rapid rotation of the drum

questions.explanation: Rapid rotation produces a centrifugal effect that drives water out through drum openings, reducing moisture before drying.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What creates the pressure difference in a vacuum cleaner?

options.B: A compressor

questions.explanation: A motor-driven fan creates a pressure difference that produces airflow, carrying dust and debris into a collection chamber or bag.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What three heat transfer mechanisms does a thermos flask address?

options.B: Only conduction

questions.explanation: A vacuum between walls reduces conduction and convection; reflective surfaces reduce radiation; an insulating stopper limits heat exchange through the neck.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why does a steel ship float?

options.A: Because steel is less dense than water
options.B: Because its hollow shape makes its average density less than the density of displaced water

questions.explanation: Its hollow shape makes its average density, including enclosed air, less than the density of the displaced water; the buoyant force balances its weight.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the role of the coil in a loudspeaker?

options.B: An electrical audio signal drives the coil in a magnetic field, moving a diaphragm

questions.explanation: An electrical audio signal drives a coil in a magnetic field, moving a diaphragm that produces pressure waves in air.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What type of image does a concave lens usually form for a real object?

options.B: Virtual, erect and diminished

questions.explanation: A concave lens diverges parallel rays and usually forms a virtual, erect and diminished image for a real object.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What factors influence exposure in a camera?

options.B: Only the lens focal length

questions.explanation: A lens focuses light onto a photosensitive sensor or film; aperture, shutter time and sensitivity influence exposure.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the power factor affect in an AC circuit?

options.B: Real power depends also on power factor in AC systems

questions.explanation: For a DC circuit, P = VI; for AC systems, real power depends also on power factor.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How many joules equal one kilowatt-hour?
questions.explanation: The energy used by a 1 kW device operating for one hour equals 3.6 million joules (3.6 × 10⁶ J).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which molecules escape during evaporation?

options.B: Higher-energy molecules

questions.explanation: Higher-energy molecules escape from a liquid surface, reducing the average kinetic energy of the remaining liquid.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why is lightning seen before thunder is heard?

options.B: Because light travels vastly faster than sound
options.C: Because sound travels faster than light
options.D: Because lightning is brighter than thunder is loud

questions.explanation: Light travels vastly faster than sound, so the flash reaches an observer before the sound wave.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What causes a metal object to become hot when current passes through it?

options.B: Electrical resistance converting electrical energy into heat

questions.explanation: Electrical resistance converts electrical energy into heat, described by Joule heating.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the principle behind an electric generator?

options.B: Electromagnetic induction

questions.explanation: Electromagnetic induction: changing magnetic flux through a coil induces an electromotive force.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What technology do automated sphygmomanometers use?

options.B: Electronic sensors

questions.explanation: Automated versions of sphygmomanometers use electronic sensors.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the reading of a Geiger counter depend on?

options.A: Only the colour of the radiation source
options.B: Radiation type, energy and instrument calibration
options.C: Only the temperature of the room
options.D: Only the distance from the source

questions.explanation: Readings depend on radiation type, energy and instrument calibration.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does a potentiometer measure in classical measurement?

options.B: It can compare or measure potential difference accurately with negligible current drawn at balance

questions.explanation: A potentiometer is a variable voltage divider; in classical measurement it can compare or measure potential difference accurately with negligible current drawn at balance.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the difference between accuracy and precision in measurement?

options.A: Accuracy is closeness among repeated measurements; precision is closeness to the true value
options.B: Accuracy is closeness to the true or accepted value; precision is closeness among repeated measurements

questions.explanation: Accuracy is closeness to the true or accepted value; precision is closeness among repeated measurements.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: According to the second law of thermodynamics, what is impossible for a heat engine?

options.B: Converting all absorbed heat into work in a cycle

questions.explanation: According to the second law, no heat engine can convert all absorbed heat into work in a cycle.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: According to the third law of thermodynamics, what is true about absolute zero?

options.B: It cannot be reached by a finite sequence of processes
options.C: It is the highest possible temperature

questions.explanation: Absolute zero cannot be reached by a finite sequence of processes.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Snell's law relate?

options.A: The angles of incidence and refraction to the refractive indices
options.B: The intensity of light to distance
options.C: The frequency of light to wavelength
options.D: The speed of light to temperature

questions.explanation: Snell's law relates the sines of the angles to the refractive indices: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does Mendel's law of segregation ensure about gametes?

options.B: Each gamete receives one allele of a gene

questions.explanation: The two alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation, so each gamete receives one allele; fertilisation restores the pair.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the law of definite proportions imply about a pure compound?

options.B: It contains its constituent elements in fixed proportions by mass regardless of source

questions.explanation: A pure chemical compound contains its constituent elements in fixed proportions by mass, regardless of its source or preparation.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What mechanisms contribute to biological evolution?

options.B: Mutation, natural selection, genetic drift, gene flow and recombination

questions.explanation: Evolution occurs through mechanisms including mutation, natural selection, genetic drift, gene flow and recombination.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What happens to the refrigerant in the evaporator of a refrigerator?

options.B: It evaporates and absorbs heat from the cabinet

questions.explanation: The refrigerant evaporates in the evaporator and absorbs heat from the cabinet.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What happens to the refrigerant in the condenser of a refrigerator?

options.B: It condenses and releases heat to the surroundings

questions.explanation: The refrigerant is compressed, condenses outside the cabinet and releases heat to the surroundings.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the principle of a hydrometer?

options.A: It floats at a depth determined by liquid density
options.B: It uses electrical resistance

questions.explanation: A hydrometer measures the relative density or specific gravity of liquids by floating at a depth determined by liquid density.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why should resistance normally be measured with the circuit de-energised?

options.A: To protect the ohmmeter and obtain accurate readings
options.B: Because resistance changes with current
options.D: Because resistance cannot be measured in live circuits under any circumstances

questions.explanation: Resistance should normally be measured with the circuit de-energised and isolated, generally using an internal source.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the SI unit of solid angle?

options.B: Steradian

questions.explanation: The SI unit of angle is the radian (rad); the solid-angle unit is steradian (sr).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does one becquerel equal?

options.B: One nuclear transformation per second

questions.explanation: The becquerel (Bq) equals one nuclear transformation per second.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does one gray equal?

options.B: One joule per kilogram

questions.explanation: The gray (Gy) equals one joule per kilogram.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What does the sievert account for?

options.B: Radiation type and, for effective dose, tissue sensitivity
options.C: Only the mass of the person

questions.explanation: The sievert (Sv) accounts for radiation type and, for effective dose, tissue sensitivity.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the function of the thermostat in a refrigerator?

options.A: It controls the compressor based on temperature
options.B: It filters the air

questions.explanation: The thermostat senses temperature and controls the cooling system to maintain the selected temperature range.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In Bernoulli's principle, what happens to static pressure when fluid speed increases (elevation unchanged)?

options.B: Static pressure decreases

questions.explanation: For steady, incompressible, non-viscous flow along a streamline, higher fluid speed is associated with lower static pressure when elevation is unchanged.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the mathematical form of Boyle's law?

options.B: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂

questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the mathematical form of Charles's law?

options.B: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂

questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of gas at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the mathematical form of Gay-Lussac's pressure law?

options.B: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂

questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of gas at constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature: P₁/T₁ = P₂/T₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the mathematical form of Ohm's law?

options.B: P = VI

questions.explanation: Ohm's law states that for a conductor under constant physical conditions, current is proportional to potential difference: V = IR.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the mathematical form of Joule's law of heating?

options.B: Q = I²RT

questions.explanation: Joule's law of heating states that electrical energy converted to heat in a resistor is Q = I²RT; equivalently Q = VIT for a suitable constant-voltage circuit.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the mathematical form of Newton's second law for constant mass?

options.B: F = ma

questions.explanation: Newton's second law states that the net force equals the rate of change of momentum; for constant mass, F = ma.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct safety practice for a pressure cooker?

options.A: Block the vent to increase pressure
options.B: Never block the vent or tamper with safety components
options.C: Remove the safety valve for faster cooking
options.D: Overfill the cooker beyond the maximum mark

questions.explanation: Never block the vent or tamper with safety components. The safety valve and gasket regulate pressure and provide sealing and pressure-release functions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about RO water purifiers?

options.A: RO removes all contaminants under all conditions
options.B: RO can reduce many dissolved substances, but performance depends on membrane, pretreatment, maintenance and water chemistry
options.D: RO adds dissolved salts to water

questions.explanation: RO can reduce many dissolved substances, but performance depends on membrane, pretreatment, maintenance and water chemistry.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about the condenser of a refrigerator?

options.A: It absorbs heat from the cabinet
options.B: It releases heat removed from the cabinet plus compressor energy to the surroundings

questions.explanation: The condenser releases heat removed from the cabinet plus the energy supplied to run the compressor.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why do air conditioner filters need regular cleaning?

options.B: To maintain airflow and indoor air quality and prevent reduced efficiency

questions.explanation: Clean filters maintain airflow and indoor air quality and help prevent reduced efficiency and unnecessary energy use.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about metal utensils in a microwave oven?

options.A: Metal is always safe in microwave ovens
options.B: Metal can reflect microwaves and may cause arcing or damage depending on shape and oven design
options.D: Metal absorbs microwaves without any effect

questions.explanation: Metal can reflect microwaves and may cause arcing or damage depending on shape and oven design. Only microwave-safe cookware should be used.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about the boiling point of water and altitude?

options.A: Water boils at a higher temperature at high altitude
options.B: Water boils at a lower temperature at high altitude because atmospheric pressure is lower
options.C: Altitude does not affect boiling point
options.D: Water does not boil at high altitude

questions.explanation: Lower atmospheric pressure reduces the boiling temperature at which water's vapour pressure equals the surrounding pressure.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why does a wet cloth feel cool in moving air?

options.B: Airflow speeds evaporation, which removes latent heat from the cloth

questions.explanation: Airflow speeds evaporation, which removes latent heat from the cloth and nearby surface.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about the sphygmomanometer?

options.B: It measures blood pressure, traditionally using an inflatable cuff and pressure gauge

questions.explanation: A sphygmomanometer measures blood pressure, traditionally using an inflatable cuff and pressure gauge; automated versions use electronic sensors.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the correct statement about a multimeter?

options.B: It combines functions such as measuring voltage, current and resistance; some models also measure continuity, capacitance, frequency or temperature

questions.explanation: A multimeter combines functions such as measuring voltage, current and resistance; some models also measure continuity, capacitance, frequency or temperature.

questions.subject: General Science
